exercises.heading: Section 6.1 Exercises
exercises.paragraph: In the following exercises, state whether each statement is true, or give an example to show that it is false.

solution.paragraph: True. If a series converges then its terms tend to zero.

problem.paragraph: $$\sum\limits_{n = 1}^{\infty}{a_{n}x^{n}}$$ converges at $$x = 0$$ for any real numbers $$a_{n}.$$
Given any sequence $$a_{n},$$ there is always some $$R > 0,$$ possibly very small, such that $$\sum\limits_{n = 1}^{\infty}{a_{n}x^{n}}$$ converges on $$\left( {-R,R} \right).$$

solution.paragraph: False. It would imply that $$anxn\to 0anxn\to 0$$ for $$|x|<R.|x|<R.$$ If $$an=nn,an=nn,$$ then $$anxn=(nx)nanxn=(nx)n$$ does not tend to zero for any $$x\ne 0.x\ne 0.$$

problem.paragraph: If $$\sum\limits_{n = 1}^{\infty}{a_{n}x^{n}}$$ has radius of convergence $$R > 0$$ and if $$\left| b_{n} \right| \leq \left| a_{n} \right|$$ for all n, then the radius of convergence of $$\sum\limits_{n = 1}^{\infty}{b_{n}x^{n}}$$ is greater than or equal to R.

Suppose that $$\sum\limits_{n = 0}^{\infty}{a_{n}\left( {x - 3} \right)^{n}}$$ converges at $$x = 6.$$ At which of the following points might the series diverge? Use the fact that if $$\sum{a_{n}\left( {x - c} \right)^{n}}$$ converges at x, then it converges at any point closer to c than x.

Suppose that $$\sum\limits_{n = 0}^{\infty}{a_{n}\left( {x + 1} \right)^{n}}$$ converges at $$x = -2.$$ At which of the following points must the series also converge? Use the fact that if $$\sum{a_{n}\left( {x - c} \right)^{n}}$$ converges at x, then it converges at any point closer to c than x.

exercises.paragraph: In the following exercises, find the radius of convergence R and interval of convergence for $$\sum{a_{n}x^{n}}$$ with the given coefficients $$a_{n}.$$

$$an=n2nan=n2n$$ so $$an+1xan\to x2an+1xan\to x2$$ so $$R=2.R=2.$$ When $$x=\pm 2x=\pm 2$$ the series diverges by the divergence test. The interval of convergence is $$I=(-2,2).I=(-2,2).$$
$$an=n22nan=n22n$$ so $$R=2.R=2.$$ When $$x=\pm 2x=\pm 2$$ the series diverges by the divergence test. The interval of convergence is $$I=(-2,2).I=(-2,2).$$

$$ak=\pi kk\pi ak=\pi kk\pi$$ so $$R=1\pi .R=1\pi .$$ When $$x=\pm 1\pi x=\pm 1\pi$$ the series is an absolutely convergent p-series. The interval of convergence is $$I=[-1\pi ,1\pi ].I=[-1\pi ,1\pi ].$$

problem.paragraph: Explain why, if $$\left| a_{n} \right|^{1/n}\rightarrow r > 0,$$ then $$\left| {a_{n}x^{n}} \right|^{1/n}\rightarrow|x|r < 1$$ whenever $$|x| < \frac{1}{r}$$ and, therefore, the radius of convergence of $$\sum\limits_{n = 1}^{\infty}{a_{n}x^{n}}$$ is $$R = \frac{1}{r}.$$

solution.paragraph: $$|anxn|1/n=|an|1/n|x|\to |x|r|anxn|1/n=|an|1/n|x|\to |x|r$$ as $$n\to \infty n\to \infty$$ and $$|x|r<1|x|r<1$$ when $$|x|<1r.|x|<1r.$$ Therefore, $$\sum n=1\infty anxn\sum n=1\infty anxn$$ converges when $$|x|<1r|x|<1r$$ by the nth root test.
$$an=(n1/n-1)nan=(n1/n-1)n$$ so $$(an)1/n\to 0(an)1/n\to 0$$ so $$R=\infty R=\infty$$

problem.paragraph: Suppose that $$p(x) = {\sum\limits_{n = 0}^{\infty}{a_{n}x^{n}}}$$ such that $$a_{n} = 0$$ if n is even. Explain why $$p(x) = - p\left( {-x} \right).$$
Suppose that $$p(x) = {\sum\limits_{n = 0}^{\infty}{a_{n}x^{n}}}$$ such that $$a_{n} = 0$$ if n is odd. Explain why $$p(x) = p\left( {-x} \right).$$

solution.paragraph: We can rewrite $$p(x)=\sum n=0\infty a2n+1x2n+1p(x)=\sum n=0\infty a2n+1x2n+1$$ and $$p(x)=p(-x)p(x)=p(-x)$$ since only even powers of $$xx$$ remain, $$p(x)p(x)$$ is an even function, for which, by definition $$p(x)=p(-x)p(x)=p(-x)$$ .

problem.paragraph: Suppose that $$p(x) = {\sum\limits_{n = 0}^{\infty}{a_{n}x^{n}}}$$ converges on $$\left( {-1,1} \right\rbrack.$$ Find the interval of convergence of $$p\left( {Ax} \right).$$
Suppose that $$p(x) = {\sum\limits_{n = 0}^{\infty}{a_{n}x^{n}}}$$ converges on $$\left( {-1,1} \right\rbrack.$$ Find the interval of convergence of $$p\left( {2x - 1} \right).$$

solution.paragraph: If $$x\in [0,1],x\in [0,1],$$ then $$y=2x-1\in [-1,1]y=2x-1\in [-1,1]$$ so $$p(2x-1)=p(y)=\sum n=0\infty anynp(2x-1)=p(y)=\sum n=0\infty anyn$$ converges.

exercises.paragraph: In the following exercises, suppose that $$p(x) = {\sum\limits_{n = 0}^{\infty}{a_{n}x^{n}}}$$ satisfies $$\underset{n\rightarrow\infty}{\lim }\frac{a_{n + 1}}{a_{n}} = 1$$ where $$a_{n} \geq 0$$ for each n. State whether each series converges on the full interval $$\left( {-1,1} \right),$$ or if there is not enough information to draw a conclusion. Use the comparison test when appropriate.

solution.paragraph: Converges on $$(-1,1)(-1,1)$$ by the ratio test

problem.paragraph: $$\sum\limits_{n = 0}^{\infty}{a_{n^{2}}x^{n^{2}}}$$ (Hint: Let $$b_{k} = a_{k}$$ if $$k = n^{2}$$ for some n, otherwise $$b_{k} = 0.)$$

solution.paragraph: Consider the series $$\sum bkxk\sum bkxk$$ where $$bk=akbk=ak$$ if $$k=n2k=n2$$ and $$bk=0bk=0$$ otherwise. Then $$bk\le akbk\le ak$$ and so the series converges on $$(-1,1)(-1,1)$$ by the comparison test.

problem.paragraph: Suppose that $$p(x)$$ is a polynomial of degree N. Find the radius and interval of convergence of $${\sum\limits_{n = 1}^{\infty}{p(n)x^{n}}}.$$

[T] Plot the graphs of $$\frac{1}{1 - x}$$ and of the partial sums $$S_{N} = {\sum\limits_{n = 0}^{N}x^{n}}$$ for $$n = 10,20,30$$ on the interval $$\left\lbrack {-0.99,0.99} \right\rbrack.$$ Comment on the approximation of $$\frac{1}{1 - x}$$ by $$S_{N}$$ near $$x = -1$$ and near $$x = 1$$ as N increases.

solution.paragraph: The approximation is more accurate near $$x=-1.x=-1.$$ The partial sums follow $$11-x11-x$$ more closely as N increases but are never accurate near $$x=1x=1$$ since the series diverges there.

problem.paragraph: [T] Plot the graphs of $$-\ln \left( {1 - x} \right)$$ and of the partial sums $$S_{N} = {\sum\limits_{n = 1}^{N}\frac{x^{n}}{n}}$$ for $$n = 10,50,100$$ on the interval $$\left\lbrack {-0.99,0.99} \right\rbrack.$$ Comment on the behavior of the sums near $$x = -1$$ and near $$x = 1$$ as N increases.

[T] Plot the graphs of the partial sums $$S_{n} = {\sum\limits_{n = 1}^{N}\frac{x^{n}}{n^{2}}}$$ for $$n = 10,50,100$$ on the interval $$\left\lbrack {-0.99,0.99} \right\rbrack.$$ Comment on the behavior of the sums near $$x = -1$$ and near $$x = 1$$ as N increases.

solution.paragraph: The approximation appears to stabilize quickly near both $$x=\pm 1.x=\pm 1.$$

problem.paragraph: [T] Plot the graphs of the partial sums $$S_{N} = {\sum\limits_{n = 1}^{N}{\sin nx^{n}}}$$ for $$n = 10,50,100$$ on the interval $$\left\lbrack {-0.99,0.99} \right\rbrack.$$ Comment on the behavior of the sums near $$x = -1$$ and near $$x = 1$$ as N increases.

[T] Plot the graphs of the partial sums $$S_{N} = {\sum\limits_{n = 0}^{N}{(-1)^{n}\frac{x^{2n + 1}}{\left( {2n + 1} \right) \text{!} }}}$$ for $$n = 3,5,10$$ on the interval $$\left\lbrack {-2\pi,2\pi} \right\rbrack.$$ Comment on how these plots approximate $$\sin x$$ as N increases.

solution.paragraph: The polynomial curves have roots close to those of $$sinxsinx$$ up to their degree and then the polynomials diverge from $$sinx.sinx.$$

problem.paragraph: [T] Plot the graphs of the partial sums $$S_{N} = {\sum\limits_{n = 0}^{N}{(-1)^{n}\frac{x^{2n}}{\left( {2n} \right) \text{!} }}}$$ for $$n = 3,5,10$$ on the interval $$\left\lbrack {-2\pi,2\pi} \right\rbrack.$$ Comment on how these plots approximate $$\cos x$$ as N increases.
